questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to live in a city where I had never been to before and which was not as well known as say, other big European cities. The idea of living in a post communist country also intrigued me. Additionally Warsaw’s history and famous classical music and arts scene was a factor I took into account. So yes, culture and history.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The city was a 10 the university was a 4, so 7 average….

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn’t too hard. I think we got a very descriptive pdf with necessary info. Housing was also clearly communicated and offered to us by the university as well. I still ported for a more private housing option, which was easy enough to find online. The location and rooms of the courses took a while to understand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The general location of our campuses. Night life information. Course content… the usual

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The SD students and their student representatives did a really good job. Thumbs up to them for all of their organizing and efforts.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Off campus if privacy is important to you. The on campus option lbs offered by the university are shared rooms. If you wanna save a lot of money do that. But if you want some comforts, especially after Copenhagen, there are ok affordable places online. Just know, that as Erasmus students only staying for 5-6 months, you will be charged more by tenants because they now we are somewhat funded. If you have polish contacts, as them about available rooms or if they can post you on their instagram.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: More expensive, but also you can life with your friends from Copenhagen! So it can be very cozy and not lonely. Recommend 100%

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I looked at the options and nope, not doing that. They looks outdated, a bit dirty and just no privacy. Only perk is that one of them is located 50m from the main campus (geology)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Simple enough. Great that you can try them out before making final decisions. Copenhagen could learn from this!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got a pdf, very clear imo. Only complicated thing was that we were registered far too late and missed out on really interesting sounding electives. Left with the “leftovers”.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Adam

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Straight forward. Can’t go wrong

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Listen to the feedback of courses from previous students. The workload is not always the same in each course. Everything is group work so be ready to work with people who will often not carry their own load. Be patient and understanding of each other's circumstances but also don't let people take advantage of this to not do anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Didn’t learn much…. Only valuable course was environmental economics. The rest was a repeat… very basic. Boring teaching, reading of PP, English was not great. 

Electives were better.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
They were ok. Some were much too easy (too superficial when trying to be interdisciplinary). Find ways in which each persons strength/background can be best utilised without being to specific.

Repetition in most cases of what we already knew or had in Copenhagen.

MERSI course has potential, but the robot talking of one lecturer and the lack of hands on application ruined it.

Environmental economics was badly taught (lecture section just read of the board) but the exercises were well taught.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Miles apart…
No space for discussions sometimes
Monotone teaching 
Hectic at times. 
Not deep enough.
Not critical enough
Law was a joke…

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the city:
Music 
Opera
Parks
Clubs
Running club
Eat as much as you can
Flea market

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Challenge the teachers more. Establish from the beginning what you expect. What YOU want to learn. What you don’t want… group work all the time?

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Travelled to other places in Poland 
Music scene is amazing
Finally being able to go out and eat/drink without breaking the bank
Classical music events and the opera 
Great museums 
Runs in the parks and along the Vistula River

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Winter
Bad lectures
The old geology faculty and the standard of the classrooms 
Bad internet
